title: Audit log enrichment: add RBAC v2 authorization decision context + role info (SIEM-stable schema)
creator: Marcus Lin
description:
Goal
Enrich Redwood audit log events with authorization (authz) decision context from RBAC v2 so that enterprise customers and internal responders can answer: who attempted what, on which resource, which policy/role allowed/denied it, and why. Ensure the resulting event schema is stable and backward compatible for SIEM export (Splunk/Datadog/Sentinel), and works across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Background / Problem
RBAC v2 introduces a unified policy evaluation path. Today, audit logs capture actor + action at a coarse level, but do not reliably include:
- allow/deny decision for every sensitive action
- which permission was evaluated (resource/action/scope)
- policy bundle version in effect
- roles/role IDs used for evaluation
- standardized reason codes for denies (to debug without leaking sensitive details)

This blocks:
- SOC 2 / ISO evidence expectations (GRC needs explicit decision + attribution)
- enterprise security questionnaires (separation of duties, least privilege enforcement)
- incident response (distinguish auth failures vs misconfig vs attempted escalation)
- SIEM detections (e.g., repeated denies on org settings, key creation attempts)

Scope
In-scope
- Control-plane + console backend audit events for all endpoints classified P0/P1 in the permission inventory
- Add authz decision envelope fields (stable, optional) to existing event schema
- Update audit-log-exporter mappings to include new fields
- Provide example events + schema documentation snippets for internal consumption

Out-of-scope (this ticket)
- Changing retention policies
- Data-plane token-level inference authorization logging beyond tenant/project scoping
- Reworking identity provider integrations (SSO/SAML), except to surface resolved role IDs in decision context

Proposed schema additions (backward compatible)
Add an optional top-level object prefix (flattened in storage/export) with "authz_*" keys to avoid nested schema requirements in downstream systems.

New fields (all optional; present when an authz check occurred):
- authz_decision: "allow" | "deny" | "error" (error = evaluator failed; request typically fails closed)
- authz_permission: canonical RBAC v2 permission string, e.g. "org.settings.update" or "api_keys.rotate"
- authz_resource_type: e.g. "org" | "project" | "dedicated_pool" | "billing_account"
- authz_resource_id: stable ID (UUID/slug). Must not include secret material.
- authz_scope: canonical scope string, e.g. "org:{org_id}" or "project:{project_id}"
- authz_policy_version: policy bundle semver/hash, e.g. "rbac-bundle@0.1.3+sha.9f3a2c1"
- authz_role_ids: comma-separated role IDs resolved for actor at evaluation time
- authz_actor_type: "user" | "service_account" | "support" | "system"
- authz_reason_code: stable enum for deny reasons (see below)
- authz_eval_ms: integer ms for evaluation latency (stringified) to monitor overhead
- authz_cache_hit: "true" | "false" (policy/role cache)

Deny reason codes (stable enums)
- ROLE_MISSING: actor has no roles in the relevant scope
- PERMISSION_MISSING: roles resolved but no allow rule matched permission
- SCOPE_MISMATCH: permission exists but not for requested resource scope
- EXPLICIT_DENY: only if we ever introduce deny rules; for now expected unused (documented)
- POLICY_NOT_FOUND: policy bundle missing / not loaded
- POLICY_VERSION_SKEW: policy bundle version incompatible with evaluator schema
- EVALUATOR_ERROR: unexpected evaluation failure
- AUTHN_CONTEXT_INVALID: actor identity context missing required claims/ids

Important constraints
- Do not log secrets: API keys, tokens, request bodies with customer prompts, SSO assertions.
- Avoid high-cardinality fields where possible, but resource_id is required for auditability; ensure SIEM guidance covers indexing.
- Schema stability: additions must be optional and non-breaking. Existing event names/types must remain unchanged.

Implementation plan
1) Define schema contract
- Align with Allison Grant on logging/trace standards (field naming, types).
- Write a short schema contract section in the audit logging spec (fields, examples, reason codes).

2) Add authz context propagation
- Ensure shared authz middleware returns a structured "DecisionContext" object.
- Plumb DecisionContext into audit log emitter for control-plane and console backend.
- Ensure correlation: reuse request_id / trace_id fields already present; do not introduce new identifiers.

3) Exporter compatibility
- Update audit-log-exporter to map new fields to SIEM targets.
- Keep exporter tolerant: if fields are missing, no failure.

4) Testing
- Golden fixtures: sample allow and deny events for key workflows (API key rotation, org settings update, billing export attempt).
- Contract tests between services and exporter (schema key presence + value shapes).
- Load/perf sanity: measure authz_eval_ms overhead; ensure within budget (<2ms p95 for cached path in hosted control plane).

Acceptance criteria
- For all P0/P1 audited endpoints under RBAC v2 enforcement, audit events include authz_decision and authz_permission.
- Deny events include authz_reason_code.
- Events include authz_policy_version and authz_role_ids when actor is role-based (user/service account). Support/system actors populated with authz_actor_type.
- No breaking schema changes: existing consumers continue to parse events.
- audit-log-exporter includes new fields in at least Splunk + Sentinel mappings, behind backward-compatible transforms.
- Documentation: internal examples of allow/deny events published in the audit logging spec page.

Notes / Open questions
- Do we log role names or only role IDs? Proposal: IDs only (stable, less sensitive), role names can change; exporter/UI can join if needed.
- For shadow mode (dual-eval), do we log both RBAC v1 and v2 decisions? Proposal: log only enforced decision in audit event, and emit metrics for shadow denies separately to avoid confusing SIEM detections.
- For Private air-gapped: policy_version should reflect the bundle installed locally; ensure consistent formatting across tiers.

Related work
- Shared authz lib and caching: ENG-5384
- Service integrations: ENG-5385, ENG-5386
- Migration dual-eval + metrics: ENG-5389
- Threat model: ENG-5390

References
- GitHub: redwood PRs for authz types/middleware + structured error codes (links in eng channel)
- GitHub: audit-log-exporter update to include authz fields (planned/ongoing)
- Confluence: Audit logging spec for authz decisions (owned by Kevin Osei / reviewed by GRC)
comments: 2025-02-05 (Kevin Osei): Drafted field list + deny reason codes. Main concern is keeping exports flat (no nested JSON) because some SIEM customers rely on rigid CSV-like ingestion paths.

2025-02-07 (Allison Grant): +1 on flat keys. Please keep naming consistent with existing audit fields (snake_case). Also ensure authz_eval_ms is emitted as a numeric-looking string; some pipelines coerce types unpredictably.

2025-02-11 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Authz middleware now returns a DecisionContext struct (decision, permission, scope, roles, policy_version). We can attach it to request context for audit emitter to consume. Need to confirm support-impersonation path populates actor_type correctly.

2025-02-14 (Olga Petrov): For SOC 2 evidence, we specifically need policy version + roles used for decision. Reason codes are helpful but avoid anything that reveals internal policy structure beyond permission names.

2025-02-18 (Sean Gallagher): Please ensure break-glass elevated sessions generate distinct audit events and include authz_decision fields too. On-call needs to see "why" a deny happened (ROLE_MISSING vs SCOPE_MISMATCH) without reading app logs.
2025-02-24 (Kevin Osei): Implemented emitter changes in control plane + console backend. Added fixtures for allow/deny on api_keys.rotate and org.sso.update. Next: exporter mapping + contract tests.

2025-03-03 (Connor O'Brien): During dual-eval rollout, we should avoid logging shadow results into audit events (would create noisy denies in SIEM). Please keep shadow-deny metrics only; audit log should reflect enforced behavior.
2025-03-06 (Marcus Lin): Reviewed schema. Request: make AUTHN_CONTEXT_INVALID distinct from EVALUATOR_ERROR so we can alert on missing identity claims regressions during rollout.
2025-03-07 (Kevin Osei): Moved to In Review. Exporter PR ready; waiting on final approval from GRC that role_ids-only is acceptable for enterprise questionnaires.
